fixtures.preview: United face Cesc Fàbregas's Como on Champions League matchday 3 (3:45am Thursday in Sydney) with nine players unavailable and Michael Carrick under pressure.
talking_points: United are winless in five Premier League games after a 1-1 draw at Leeds and lost 2-0 at Atlético Madrid last week.
Out: Martínez (thigh), Mainoo (about 10 more days), Shaw, Heaven (ill), Sesko (shin relapse), Dorgu, Ugarte; Yoro is suspended after his red card at Atlético.
Marcus Rashford missed training with a hip issue and is a doubt, per Carrick.
Como beat Leipzig 4-1 and lost 3-2 at Feyenoord, but are missing Kean, Chalobah and Jesús Rodríguez; Fàbregas says he doesn't believe in crises.

fixtures.preview: A Sunday 2pm home game against Bournemouth, moved from Saturday for UK TV; United will be looking for their first league win in six.
A lunchtime trip to Stamford Bridge with a 12:30pm UK start.
Matchday 4 of the Champions League league phase brings Roma to Old Trafford.
A Sunday 4:30pm UK home game against Aston Villa, picked for TV.
Sydney's second game of the season, at home on Sunday afternoon against the team that beat them 2-1 here in February.
talking_points: Sydney drew 0-0 with the Wanderers in the season opener, a game described as drab with little attacking quality.
Adelaide won 2-1 at Allianz Stadium when the sides last met on 14 February.
Patrick Kisnorbo is Sydney's head coach; no team news for Sunday was found.
It is an A-Leagues double-header, with Sydney FC Women v Melbourne City at 5:45pm in the same stadium.

fixtures.preview: A 5pm Halloween game at AAMI Park, Melbourne City's official home opener.
A Friday-night home game against the Mariners.
An away trip to Brisbane Roar at Kayo Stadium, 6:40pm Brisbane time (7:40pm Sydney).
